newsitem.title: USA: UPR faces long wait for Pennzoil without cash bid.
newsitem.headline: UPR faces long wait for Pennzoil without cash bid.

text.p: Despite its apparently generous terms, Union Pacific Resources Group Inc's hostile bid for Pennzoil Co faces severe problems and many investors say if UPR wants to clinch the deal it will have to go all-cash.
The initial offer is valued by UPR at $84 per share, a 41 percent premium to the pre-bid price, but Pennzoil has so far been able to deflect the aggressor's arguments.
It characterizes UPR's cash first and stock later offer as coercive, forcing shareholders to accept for fear of something worse -- receiving UPR stock in the second portion.
Holders of UPR stock will also face 50 percent earnings per share dilution in the first year if the deal goes through.

"It does appear to be a good price and Pennzoil has problems defending itself against the total price, but the stock part is difficult to swallow," said one fund manager with a large holding of Pennzoil stock.
The first test of shareholder sentiment comes on July 21, when the tender offer first closes.
